The re-render storm
One state change re-renders every child
function App() {   const [count, setCount] = useState(0);   return (     <>       <Navbar />       <ProductList />       <CartIcon count={count} />       <Footer />     </>   ); }
Only CartIcon uses count — yet React re-runs all four children by default.
Three tools, three things they remember
React.memo
remembers
a rendered component
Skips re-rendering when every prop is equal to last time.
React.memo(Footer)
useMemo
remembers
a computed value
Skips recalculating until a dependency changes.
useMemo(() => calc(a), [a])
useCallback
remembers
a function
Returns the same function reference until a dependency changes.
useCallback(fn, [a])
React.memo
Skip a child when its props haven't changed
const Navbar = React.memo(function Navbar() {   return <nav>…</nav>; }); // same for ProductList, CartIcon, Footer
Before rendering, memo compares each prop with ===. All equal → reuse last result.
CartIcon still renders — its count prop really changed. That's correct.
The catch
memo compares by reference — and every render makes new objects
Prop type
Example
Same next render?
Keep it stable with
Primitive
"shoes", 42, true
Yes — compared by value
nothing needed
Object / array
{ veg: true }, [1, 2]
No — new reference
useMemo
Function
(id) => add(id)
No — new reference
useCallback
JSX children
<h2>Hi</h2>
No — new element
useMemo
{} === {} // false
(() => {}) === (() => {}) // false
The trap
A new function every render breaks memo
function App() {   const [count, setCount] = useState(0);   // created again on EVERY render   const addToCart = (id) => { … };   return <ProductList onAdd={addToCart} />; }
Watch ProductList: it has memo, but onAdd is fn#2, fn#3, fn#4… a "new" prop each time, so memo never skips.
useMemo
Remember a computed value
// Job 1: skip an expensive calculation const visible = useMemo(   () => products     .filter(p => p.price <= maxPrice)     .sort(byRating),   [products, maxPrice] );
// Job 2: keep an object's reference stable const filters = useMemo(   () => ({ veg, rating }), [veg, rating] );
On every render, React checks the dependencies:
Same as last time
Return the cached value. Function not called.
Something changed
Run the function again, cache the new result.
Typing in an unrelated box? Dependencies unchanged → no re-filtering.
useCallback
Remember a function — and memo works again
const addToCart = useCallback((id) => {   setCart(c => [...c, id]); }, []); // same fn#1 on every render <ProductList onAdd={addToCart} />
Now onAdd stays fn#1. memo sees equal props, so ProductList is skipped.
The pair works as a team: memo on the child, useCallback in the parent.
useMemo vs useCallback
useMemo
Stores the cooked meal
const total = useMemo(   () => calcTotal(cart),   [cart] ); // total → 1499 (a value)
Calls your function and keeps the result.
useCallback
Stores the recipe card
const onBuy = useCallback(   () => checkout(cart),   [cart] ); // onBuy → ƒ (not called yet)
Keeps the function itself, uncalled.
useCallback(fn, deps) is the same as useMemo(() => fn, deps)

useMemo
When not to memoize
It's already cheap
Summing 10 cart items or rendering a small button costs less than the memo bookkeeping.
Props change anyway
If a prop changes on every render, memo compares and then renders anyway: pure overhead.
Wrong dependencies
A missing dependency gives stale data. A faster wrong answer is still a bug.
Measure first: React DevTools → Profiler, or turn on "Highlight updates when components render".

12 real-world bugs

Q1 · Amazon-style product page
Each time the cart count changes, the heavy Footer (no props, 200 links) re-renders. What stops it?
function App() {   const [cartCount, setCartCount] = useState(0);   return (     <>       <Header cartCount={cartCount} />       <Footer />     </>   ); }
A  React.memo on Footer
B  useMemo for cartCount
C  useCallback for setCartCount
D  Move Footer into Header
Q1 · Answer
Wrap Footer in React.memo
const Footer = React.memo(function Footer() {   return <footer>…200 links…</footer>; });
How it works
Footer has no props, so old props and new props are always equal.
memo sees "nothing changed" and reuses the last render. Header still renders — it needs cartCount.
A · React.memo
Before: Footer renders on every cart change
After: Footer skipped
Q2 · Flipkart search page
Toggling dark mode lags: 20,000 products are filtered and sorted again on every render. Fix?
function SearchPage({ products }) {   const [query, setQuery] = useState("");   const [dark, setDark] = useState(false);   const results = products     .filter(p => p.name.includes(query))     .sort(byPrice);   return <Results items={results} dark={dark} />; }
A  React.memo on Results
B  useMemo for results
C  useCallback for results
D  Store results in useState
Q2 · Answer
Cache the filtered list with useMemo
const results = useMemo(   () => products     .filter(p => p.name.includes(query))     .sort(byPrice),   [products, query] );
How it works
results is a computed value, so useMemo is the tool.
Toggling dark changes neither products nor query, so the cached array comes back instantly.
memo on Results alone wouldn't help: the 20,000-item filter still runs in SearchPage.
B · useMemo
Before: filter + sort on every render
After: only when query or products change
Q3 · Instagram feed
Post is already wrapped in React.memo, yet every Post re-renders when the notification badge updates. Fix?
const Post = React.memo(PostCard); function Feed({ posts }) {   const [badge, setBadge] = useState(0);   const handleLike = (id) => likePost(id);   return posts.map(p =>     <Post key={p.id} post={p} onLike={handleLike} />   ); }
A  Wrap Feed in React.memo
B  useMemo for posts
C  useCallback for handleLike
D  Remove the key prop
Q3 · Answer
Give memo a stable onLike
const handleLike = useCallback(   (id) => likePost(id),   [] );
How it works
Without it, handleLike is a brand-new function each render, so memo sees onLike "changed" for every Post.
useCallback hands back the same reference, so memo(Post) can finally skip.
C · useCallback
Before: every Post renders on each badge update
After: Posts skipped
Q4 · Zomato restaurant list
RestaurantList is wrapped in React.memo but still re-renders while the user types in the search box. Fix?
const RestaurantList = React.memo(List); function Home() {   const [search, setSearch] = useState("");   const [veg, setVeg] = useState(true);   return (     <RestaurantList       filters={{ veg: veg, minRating: 4 }} />   ); }
A  Add React.memo again
B  useMemo for the filters object
C  useCallback for filters
D  JSON.stringify the props
Q4 · Answer
Keep the same filters object
const filters = useMemo(   () => ({ veg: veg, minRating: 4 }),   [veg] ); <RestaurantList filters={filters} />
How it works
{ } builds a new object every render, so memo always sees a "new" prop.
useMemo returns the same object until veg changes.
It's an object, not a function → useMemo, not useCallback.
B · useMemo
Before: list renders on every keystroke
After: renders only when veg toggles
Q5 · YouTube watch page
The player updates time every second. Comments (prop: videoId only) re-renders every second too. Fix?
function WatchPage({ videoId }) {   const [time, setTime] = useState(0);   // setTime runs every 1s while playing   return (     <>       <Player time={time} />       <Comments videoId={videoId} />     </>   ); }
A  React.memo on Comments
B  useMemo for videoId
C  useCallback for setTime
D  useMemo for Player
Q5 · Answer
Memoize the Comments component
const Comments = React.memo(CommentsList);
How it works
videoId is a string — compared by value, so it's already stable. Only memo was missing.
useMemo on a string does nothing: primitives never need it.
Player keeps rendering every second — it needs time.
A · React.memo
Before: Comments renders 60× a minute
After: only when videoId changes
Q6 · Swiggy cart summary
A teammate wants to "optimize" this. The cart holds about 10 items. What's the best choice?
function CartSummary({ items }) {   const total = items.reduce(     (sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty,     0   );   return <p>Total: Rs. {total}</p>; }
A  useMemo for total
B  useCallback for reduce
C  React.memo on CartSummary
D  None — leave it as is
Q6 · Answer
Don't optimize what's already fast
// keep it simple — no hook needed const total = items.reduce(   (sum, i) => sum + i.price * i.qty,   0 );
How to think
Adding 10 numbers is nearly free.
useMemo costs memory plus a dependency check on every render — more than the work it saves here.
Optimize only what the Profiler shows is slow.
D · None needed
Rule: cheap work + simple code beats clever caching
Q7 · Google-style search suggestions
The Network tab shows the suggestions API being called again and again, forever. Fix?
function SearchBox({ query }) {   const [list, setList] = useState([]);   const fetchSuggestions = () =>     api.suggest(query).then(setList);   useEffect(() => {     fetchSuggestions();   }, [fetchSuggestions]); }
A  React.memo on SearchBox
B  useMemo for list
C  useCallback for fetchSuggestions
D  Remove the useEffect
Q7 · Answer
A function in deps must be stable
const fetchSuggestions = useCallback(   () => api.suggest(query).then(setList),   [query] ); useEffect(() => {   fetchSuggestions(); }, [fetchSuggestions]);
How it works
The loop: fetch → setList → re-render → new function → effect runs → fetch…
useCallback keeps the same function until query changes, so the effect runs once per query.
C · useCallback
Before: endless API calls
After: one call per query
Q8 · Netflix movie row
handleSelect already uses useCallback, but MovieRow still re-renders whenever the hero banner rotates. What's missing?
function Browse({ movies }) {   const [banner, setBanner] = useState(0);   const handleSelect = useCallback(     (m) => openDetails(m), []   );   return <MovieRow movies={movies}     onSelect={handleSelect} />; } function MovieRow(props) { … }
A  React.memo on MovieRow
B  useMemo for handleSelect
C  A second useCallback
D  useMemo for banner
Q8 · Answer
useCallback needs a memo child
const MovieRow = React.memo(function MovieRow(props) {   … });
How it works
A normal child re-renders whenever its parent does — it never looks at props.
useCallback only pays off when the child is memoized and compares them.
A · React.memo
useCallback alone: no effect on rendering
memo + useCallback: MovieRow skipped
Q9 · Zerodha-style stock dashboard
A clock ticks every second. The memoized PriceChart (5,000 points) redraws every second even though ticks didn't change. Fix?
const PriceChart = React.memo(Chart); function Dashboard({ ticks }) {   const [now, setNow] = useState(Date.now());   const chartData = ticks.map(t =>     ({ x: t.time, y: t.price })   );   return <PriceChart data={chartData} />; }
A  useCallback for chartData
B  useMemo for chartData
C  React.memo on Dashboard
D  Remove React.memo
Q9 · Answer
One useMemo, two wins
const chartData = useMemo(   () => ticks.map(t =>     ({ x: t.time, y: t.price })   ),   [ticks] );
How it works
Speed: the 5,000-item map runs only when ticks change.
Identity: the array keeps the same reference, so memo(PriceChart) can skip the redraw.
chartData is data, not a function → not useCallback.
B · useMemo
Before: chart redraws every second
After: redraws only on new ticks
Q10 · Gmail inbox
Clicking one email re-renders all 500 rows. What makes only the 2 affected rows re-render?
function Inbox({ emails }) {   const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState(null);   const archive = (id) => api.archive(id);   return emails.map(e =>     <EmailRow key={e.id} email={e}       selected={e.id === selectedId}       onArchive={archive} />   ); }
A  React.memo on EmailRow only
B  useCallback for archive only
C  React.memo + useCallback
D  useMemo for emails
Q10 · Answer
The team: memo on the row, useCallback in the parent
const EmailRow = React.memo(Row); const archive = useCallback(   (id) => api.archive(id),   [] );
How it works
memo lets each row compare its props. useCallback keeps onArchive the same.
Now only 2 rows have a changed selected prop: the one losing selection and the one gaining it.
Either fix alone still renders all 500.
C · memo + useCallback
Before: 500 row renders per click
After: 2 row renders per click
Q11 · Medium-style blog card
Card is wrapped in React.memo, yet it re-renders on every scroll. Its content never changes. Fix?
const Card = React.memo(CardBox); function Page() {   const [scrollY, setScrollY] = useState(0);   return (     <Card>       <h2>Top 10 React tips</h2>     </Card>   ); }
A  useMemo for the children JSX
B  useCallback for Card
C  Wrap Card in memo twice
D  memo can't work with JSX
Q11 · Answer
children is a prop too
const content = useMemo(   () => <h2>Top 10 React tips</h2>,   [] ); return <Card>{content}</Card>;
How it works
JSX creates a new element object every render, so props.children is "new" each time.
useMemo keeps the same element, so memo(Card) can skip.
Simpler option: define static JSX outside the component.
A · useMemo
Before: Card renders on every scroll event
After: Card skipped
Q12 · Checkout form
After optimizing, the Save button always saves an empty form, even after the user typed. What's the fix?
const SaveButton = React.memo(Button); function Checkout() {   const [form, setForm] = useState({});   const save = useCallback(() => {     api.save(form);   }, []);   return <SaveButton onSave={save} />; }
A  Remove React.memo
B  Add form to the deps array
C  Switch useCallback to useMemo
D  useMemo for form
Q12 · Answer
Wrong deps = stale closure
const save = useCallback(() => {   api.save(form); }, [form]);
How it works
With [] the function is created once and remembers the first form: { }.
List every value the function reads. The ESLint rule react-hooks/exhaustive-deps catches this.
An optimization must never change the result.
B · Fix the deps
Before: saves { } forever
After: saves the latest form
Which one do I reach for?
A child re-renders though its props didn't change?
React.memo
Heavy calculation — or an object / array / JSX passed to a memo child?
useMemo
A function passed to a memo child — or listed in useEffect deps?
useCallback
Already cheap and fast?
Nothing
